title: ZENO: A Type-based Optimization Framework for Zero Knowledge Neural Network Inference
problem: Zero-knowledge neural networks using zkSNARK suffer from poor performance due to million-scale circuit computation with heavy scalar-level dependencies. Circuit-level compilation lacks awareness of high-level neural network semantics, leading to suboptimal implementations.
motivation: Zero-knowledge proofs enable privacy-preserving neural network inference with computation integrity guarantees, but current implementations are too slow for practical deployment.
method: ZENO introduces a type-aware language construct that captures privacy-type and tensor-type information at the high level. It applies privacy-type driven optimizations to reduce scalar dependencies and tensor-type driven optimizations to leverage parallelism. Additional NN-centric system optimizations further accelerate the zkSNARK circuit evaluation pipeline.
key_novelty: Type-based optimization framework that uses privacy and tensor type information to guide aggressive circuit optimizations for zkSNARK neural networks.
contributions: ZENO language construct that maintains high-level semantics and type information for zero-knowledge neural networks
Privacy-type driven optimizations to reduce scalar-level dependencies in zkSNARK circuits
Tensor-type driven optimizations for aggressive circuit-level transformations
NN-centric system optimizations achieving 8.5× end-to-end speedup with VGG16 proof time reduced from 6 minutes to 48 seconds
